start.text: Lowsong's light is cold: dull horn, a black cradle, salt run down the stone in pale streaks from the gallery. Against its back a turf-roofed bothy, a water butt at the corner. The iron hook by the door is empty.
The step has gone green. Nobody has gone in and out much, these three months.
It wants a memory, like all of them. Out here the fog gives none up: it only sings.
